b: This is a dining table I designed and built for a private residence. The idea was to create a sculptural base using a series of wooden ribs that gradually change shape, creating a flowing form that looks different depending on the angle you view it from.

The base consists of 88 individual ribs made from 1" thick maple. I designed the entire piece in Rhino and CNC-cut each rib. The design is symmetrical, with 44 different rib profiles mirrored from one side of the table to the other, creating the curves and transitions throughout the structure.

For the assembly, I used a series of 1" metal tubes running through the ribs from one end to the other. I also CNC-cut temporary MDF spacers to keep the ribs evenly separated and properly aligned during assembly. Most of the ribs are held in place by friction, with a few secured using small through-screws.

The entire base was stained a walnut color and finished with water-based polyurethane. The tabletop is a single piece of 19mm thick glass, which simply rests on the wooden structure. At that size and thickness, the glass is extremely heavy, so its own weight keeps it in place.
The finished table measures 3m long, 1.4m wide, and 0.75m tall (approximately 118" × 55" × 30"). The whole project took around a month, including design, fabrication, finishing, and installation.
I've included a few pictures of the fabrication and assembly process so you can see how the structure came together.
Happy to answer any questions about the design or construction!
